name: Dak Nong
provinceNote: National Assembly Resolution 202/2025/QH15 merged Dak Nong, Binh Thuan, and former Lam Dong into a new Lam Dong province from 12 Jun 2025, with the administrative center at Da Lat. Visitor sites still print Dak Nong on their pages.
dotReason: Worth a geopark loop from the highlands
summary: The wide sheet of Dray Sap on the Serepok is the picture, and Ta Dung’s island reservoir is the other reason to stop. Sleep in Gia Nghia, on the highway crossroads, or on the Dak Som shore when the boat morning matters. Stay for a two- or three-day loop by car or motorbike. Go on to Da Lat if Lien Khuong is the flight and the cool hills are the trip. Dak Nong has no airport.
fee: No single province ticket. Gate prices are Check on arrival.
getThere: Fly to Buon Ma Thuot, then the road to Gia Nghia. Dak Nong has no airport.
bestMonths: January to early April for the roads; May to October for fuller falls
seoTitle: Dak Nong travel guide — Dray Sap and the island lake
seoDescription: Dray Sap is about 100 metres wide on the Serepok, about 110 km from Gia Nghia. Ta Dung’s islands sit about 45 km the other way. Fly to Buon Ma Thuot.
intro: Stand where the Serepok drops in one wide sheet through primary forest. UNESCO describes Dray Sap as about 100 metres across and about 12 metres down. The Dak Nong provincial handbook puts the eco-site in Dak Sor, Krong No, about 110 km from Gia Nghia, and names Gia Long and Trinh Nu in the same cluster. Give the falls a day of their own. They are not a stop you add after a Ta Dung morning.

Ta Dung is the other picture: the Dong Nai 3 reservoir at Dak Som and Dak Plao, in Dak Glong, with dozens of wooded islands. The provincial tourism portal calls it the plateau’s answer to Ha Long Bay. The handbook puts the lake about 45 km southeast of Gia Nghia on QL28. That same portal prints free entry for the Ta Dung park listing. A boat ticket and a resort ticket are separate, and those prices are Check on arrival. Cool air is the reason to sleep in Dak Som when the boat is the morning.

Gia Nghia sits on National Highway 14 and National Highway 28. Lieng Nung, a 35-metre fall inside a hexagonal basalt vault, is about 9 km out on QL28. EXPLORASOUND, on Dak Nur hill, is the sound museum UNESCO calls Vietnam’s first. The Dak Kar lithophone hall is about 9 km toward Da Lat, in Dak Nia, and the handbook calls those stones nearly 3,000 years old. Buon Buor, about 90 km toward Dak Lak, is the Ede longhouse village on the Serepok. Evenings in town are dinner and an early night.

Stay if you will hire a car or a motorbike and accept the distances. Fly into Buon Ma Thuot when the Serepok is the plan. Fly into Lien Khuong, near Da Lat, when Ta Dung and the cool hills are one trip. The mistake is stacking Krong No and the lake into the same morning, or walking into a lava tube without an authorized guide. Krong No authorities banned self-guided entry after deaths. C9, near Chu Bluk, is the tube the provincial tourism portal lists at 217 metres, with free entry on that listing. A guided surcharge is Check on arrival.
gettingAround: Dak Nong has no airport of its own. The provincial handbook puts Gia Nghia about 125 km from Buon Ma Thuot. Bao Lam Dong puts that road at about 135 km. Vexere lists about 120 km and about two hours for one limousine from Buon Ma Thuot airport to Gia Nghia, and Bao Lam Dong quotes a Hoang Kim fare of 150,000 VND on one list. Other night fares run higher. Check on arrival. From Ho Chi Minh City the handbook quotes about 250 km, about six hours, and bus fares of about 150,000–200,000 VND. Vex Sapa puts Gia Nghia to Da Lat at about 180 km and four to four and a half hours. Ta Dung is about 45 km southeast on QL28. Dray Sap is about 110 km away in Krong No. Hire a car or a motorbike for more than one stop. Whether Grab works in Gia Nghia is Check on arrival. The nearest rail station is Check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: Gia Nghia
stayAreas.summary: Town hotels and guesthouses on the highway crossroads, for Lieng Nung, the sound museum, and the long drives to Krong No.

stayAreas.name: Ta Dung lakeshore
stayAreas.summary: Lodges and homestays in Dak Som when the boat morning matters more than being in town.

eat: Com lam is sticky rice cooked in bamboo, the meal the provincial handbook and the tourism portal name at M'Nong and Ma gatherings, often with grilled fish. Grilled catfish from the Serepok is the specialty through Krong No and Cu Jut. Ruou can is a shared jar at a ceremony, not a night out.

Coffee is the flagship crop on the basalt around Gia Nghia and Dak Mil. Dak R'Mang, in Dak Glong, holds a Sunday market with Hmong traders, textiles, thang co, and corn wine. The opening hour is Check on arrival.
interestsBody: Dray Sap is the wide Serepok cascade. UNESCO describes it as about 100 metres across and about 12 metres down. The handbook puts it about 110 km from Gia Nghia, and the gate price is Check on arrival.
Ta Dung is the island reservoir, about 45 km southeast on QL28. The park listing is free. Boat and resort tickets are Check on arrival.
Krong No’s lava tubes are a guided visit. Self-guided entry is banned. C9 is the tube the tourism portal lists as free, at 217 metres. A guided surcharge is Check on arrival.
EXPLORASOUND and the Dak Kar lithophones are short stops from Gia Nghia. Buon Buor is the Ede longhouse village, about 90 km toward Dak Lak.

blocks.heading: The wide sheet
paragraphs: UNESCO describes Dray Sap as about 100 metres across and about 12 metres down, in primary forest. The provincial handbook puts the eco-site in Dak Sor, Krong No, about 110 km from Gia Nghia, and names Gia Long and Trinh Nu in the same cluster. The gate price and the official hour are Check on arrival. Foody lists 07:30–18:00 for the cluster. That listing is not a ticket office.

blocks.heading: Ta Dung
paragraphs: Ta Dung is the Dong Nai 3 reservoir at Dak Som and Dak Plao, about 45 km southeast of Gia Nghia on QL28. The provincial tourism portal calls the wooded islands the plateau’s answer to Ha Long Bay and prints free entry for the park listing. A boat ticket and a resort ticket are Check on arrival. Granite waterfall sits in the same park. Do not treat the lake as a same-day add-on from Da Lat.

blocks.heading: Lawful caves only
paragraphs: Krong No authorities banned self-guided entry to the lava tubes after deaths. Tuoi Tre reported the ban, including C7. Visit with an authorized guide. The provincial tourism portal lists cave C9, also called Hang Doi, at 217 metres, near Chu Bluk, and prints free entry for that listing. A guided surcharge is Check on arrival. Nam Kar is a roadside scoria cone on QL28 between Gia Nghia and Krong No. A fee there is Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Sound, stone, and the longhouse
paragraphs: EXPLORASOUND, on Dak Nur hill in Gia Nghia, is the sound museum UNESCO calls Vietnam’s first. The Dak Kar lithophone hall is about 9 km from central Gia Nghia on QL28 toward Da Lat, in Dak Nia. The handbook calls the Dak Kar stones nearly 3,000 years old. Hours and fees for both are Check on arrival. Buon Buor, in Tam Thang, Cu Jut, is about 90 km toward Dak Lak: Ede longhouses, weaving, and gongs on the Serepok. Lieng Nung, about 9 km from Gia Nghia, is the 35-metre fall inside a basalt vault. Its fee is Check on arrival.

body: One hired car or motorbike covers the loop. Dray Sap and Ta Dung are different days. Evenings in Gia Nghia are quiet. The provincial pages and UNESCO describe festivals and gong culture, not a bar street.

season.label: Dry roads, fuller falls
season.note: The provincial handbook favors January through early April, names coffee blossom in March and golden shower trees in May and June, and calls summer rainy with quick showers. UNESCO calls May to October the wet season, when the waterfalls run fuller. Hoi Xuan Lieng Nung is a spring gathering around Gia Nghia. The tourism portal gives no fixed Gregorian date. Long Tong, the Tay and Nung rice festival in Nam Tan, Krong No, follows the lunar calendar. One report gives the 10th day of the first lunar month, 31 January 2023. Check those dates on arrival. Storm closures on the roads are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: Should you fly into Dak Nong?
faqs.a: Dak Nong has no airport. The provincial handbook puts Gia Nghia about 125 km from Buon Ma Thuot. Bao Lam Dong puts that road at about 135 km. Vexere lists about 120 km and about two hours for one airport limousine. Lien Khuong, near Da Lat, is the other flight when Ta Dung is the plan. Vex Sapa puts Gia Nghia to Da Lat at about 180 km and four to four and a half hours. Fares and the day’s minutes are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: Can you walk into the volcanic caves on your own?
faqs.a: No. Krong No authorities banned self-guided entry after deaths. Tuoi Tre reported the ban, including C7. Go with an authorized guide. The provincial tourism portal lists C9 at 217 metres and prints free entry for that listing. A guided surcharge is Check on arrival.

faqs.q: How many days does the geopark need?
faqs.a: Two days cover Gia Nghia, a short stop such as Lieng Nung, and a Ta Dung boat morning. Add a third if Dray Sap is the plan. The handbook puts that waterfall about 110 km from Gia Nghia, so it is not the same morning as the lake.
